grade.rationale: The template is clear, semantically structured, and provides useful empty states and accessible labels. Its main weaknesses are unstable disclosure state based on array positions and an ARIA reference whose target is removed when collapsed.

summary: The usage-history dialog is generally well organized and readable. Two issues should be addressed: recent-entry expansion is keyed by a mutable array index, and collapsed entries retain aria-controls references to elements that do not exist. Test coverage is unknown, and the unavailable ESLint result does not establish a defect.

grade.rationale: Rendering and aggregation bindings appear internally consistent, but positional expansion state can select the wrong entry after the recent-entry collection changes.
The template has coherent sections and naming, although using different identity schemes for tracking, expansion, and element IDs makes future collection updates harder to reason about.
Headings, labels, empty messages, and detail terms communicate the interface clearly.
Empty aggregate and recent-entry collections are handled explicitly. Failure and loading behavior cannot be determined from this template alone.
The markup exposes useful roles and labels, but index-derived state and IDs make reorder and refresh scenarios brittle to implement and test. Coverage evidence was not supplied.

findings.title: Expanded entry state is tied to the array index
findings.description: The disclosure state compares expandedEntry() with the current loop index. If recent entries are inserted, removed, or reordered while the dialog is open, the same numeric index can refer to a different entry, causing unrelated details to appear expanded. This also conflicts with the loop's attempt to preserve entry identity through its track expression.
findings.recommendation: Store and compare a stable entry identifier, such as a guaranteed-unique ledger entry ID, and derive aria-controls and panel IDs from that identifier instead of the array index.

findings.title: Collapsed disclosures reference absent control targets
findings.description: aria-controls is always emitted on each summary button, but its referenced details element is only created while the entry is expanded. In the collapsed state, the ID reference therefore has no target in the accessibility tree or DOM.
findings.recommendation: Keep each details container in the DOM and hide it when collapsed, or only emit aria-controls while its target exists. Continue keeping aria-expanded synchronized with the visible state.
